questions.question: Dr. Meriem confides to Dr. Sofia: 'I'm exhausted, I don't know how I'm going to manage my pregnancy and my practice.' Dr. Sofia asks her if she knows her rights. Dr. Meriem answers: 'Not really.' Dr. Sofia explains to her that the Moroccan Labor Code provides for maternity leave of:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, the Moroccan Labor Code provides for 14 weeks of maternity leave (7 weeks before and 7 weeks after delivery). You are entitled to this leave, don't forget it!'

questions.question: Dr. Meriem: 'But if I stop for 14 weeks, I'm going to lose my patient base!' Dr. Sofia tells her that the fear of losing her patient base is the first barrier to maternity leave. A recent survey shows that:
options: 90% of practitioners do not take their leave
75% of practitioners fear an impact on their career
50% of practitioners permanently close their practice
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, a recent survey shows that 75% of practitioners feel that the desire for motherhood interferes with their professional project. You are not alone, and that's precisely why you need to anticipate.'

questions.question: Dr. Meriem: 'How am I going to find a replacement?' Dr. Sofia explains that replacement is a real challenge. According to a survey, what percentage of practitioners have difficulty finding a replacement?
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, 66% of practitioners have difficulty finding a replacement. It's a real problem, but there are solutions: networks, platforms, early announcements.'

questions.question: Dr. Sofia advises Meriem to anticipate her leave. She asks her: 'How long before your delivery should you start looking for a replacement?' Meriem answers: 'I don't know.' Sofia replies:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, ideally, start looking 3 to 6 months before. This gives you time to find the right person and prepare the transition.'

questions.question: Meriem wonders about the administrative procedures during her leave. Sofia explains that as a liberal professional, she must:
options: Appoint a replacement and inform patients
Continue paying her expenses without income
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, as a liberal professional, you must appoint a replacement, inform your patients by mail or email, and plan the terms of your return.'

questions.question: Meriem asks Sofia how she managed her own leave. Sofia replies that she chose to take her leave in several parts. She explains that the Labor Code allows:
options: Taking the leave all at once
Taking the leave whenever you want
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, splitting the leave is possible with agreement. This allows better management of the return and breastfeeding.'

questions.question: Meriem confides: 'I'm afraid of losing my skills during 14 weeks.' Sofia replies that skills are not lost, but it is important to:
options: Take distance training during the leave
Rest and take care of yourself
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, continuing education is important, but rest is just as important. Maternity leave is meant for rest and bonding with your child.'

questions.question: Meriem admits: 'I feel guilty leaving my practice to a replacement.' Sofia tells her that guilt is common. She advises her to:
options: Accept that it is a necessity
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, guilt is normal, but it should not prevent you from taking care of yourself. Accept that it is a necessity, trust your replacement, and rest.'

questions.question: Meriem asks: 'How can I prepare my return?' Sofia advises her to:
options: Return only when she feels ready
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, a gradual return with half-days or reduced days allows you to readjust smoothly. Don't hesitate to discuss it with your replacement.'

questions.question: Meriem asks Sofia how she managed breastfeeding and work. Sofia tells her that she arranged her practice to:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, expressing milk during breaks is a practical solution. You can also plan adapted hours for breastfeeding.'

questions.question: Meriem wonders about the financial assistance available during her leave. Sofia explains that she can benefit from:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, you can benefit from CNSS daily allowances during your maternity leave. Check with CNSS for the procedures.'

questions.question: Meriem says to Sofia: 'Will my patients accept a replacement?' Sofia replies that patient loyalty comes through:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, the key is clear communication. Inform your patients in advance, introduce them to the replacement, and reassure them about the continuity of care.'

questions.question: Meriem confides: 'I don't have an assistant to manage my absence.' Sofia advises her to:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, hiring a temporary assistant can be a solution. She can manage the administrative and reception tasks during your absence.'

questions.question: Meriem asks Sofia how she managed the stress of returning to work. Sofia replies that she took the time to:
options: Gradually adapt and allow herself breaks
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, returning to work is a key moment. You need to give yourself time, breaks, and accept that everything won't be perfect on the first day.'

questions.question: Meriem asks: 'How to manage fatigue after a difficult night with the baby?' Sofia advises her to:
options: Adjust her hours and plan breaks
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, fatigue is a real challenge. Adjust your hours, plan breaks, and don't hesitate to delegate certain tasks.'

questions.question: Meriem asks Sofia how she managed to balance family and professional life. Sofia replies that she learned to:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, the key is delegation and the art of saying no. Learn to delegate tasks to your assistant and set boundaries.'

questions.question: Meriem asks: 'What if my replacement is not satisfactory?' Sofia replies that she should:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, communication is essential. Discuss with your replacement, identify problems and look for solutions together. If nothing changes, you can plan a backup solution.'

questions.question: Meriem confides: 'I'm afraid of losing my place in the profession.' Sofia replies that:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, motherhood is not a weakness. It brings strength, sensitivity, and experience that are assets in your practice.'

questions.question: Meriem asks Sofia what resources are available for women dentists. Sofia advises her to:
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, there are networks of women dentists like the Association of Women Dentists. These networks offer support, advice, and opportunities.'

questions.question: Meriem says: 'I don't dare ask for help.' Sofia replies that:
options: Asking for help is a sign of strength
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness. Everyone needs help at some point. Don't hesitate to reach out to your colleagues.'

questions.question: Meriem asks Sofia how she prepared her return. Sofia replies that she organized:
options: A lighter schedule and messages to patients
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, I prepared my return by lightening my schedule and sending reassuring messages to my patients. This allowed me to return smoothly.'

questions.question: Meriem wonders about the impact of pregnancy on her practice. Sofia explains that:
options: She can continue working with adaptations
She must go on sick leave
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, pregnancy is not an illness. With adaptations (posture, breaks, delegation), you can continue to practice safely for you and your baby.'

questions.question: Meriem asks: 'How to manage patients' looks when I'm pregnant?' Sofia replies:
options: Talk about it openly if she wishes
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, pregnancy is wonderful news! If you feel comfortable, share it with your patients. They will be happy for you.'

questions.question: Meriem says: 'I will be missed by my patients.' Sofia replies that:
options: It's true, they will forget her
Her patients will be understanding and will wait for her
questions.explanation: Dr. Sofia: 'Meriem, your patients are loyal to you. They will understand and be happy to see you again after your leave.'

questions.question: Meriem, at the end of their conversation, says: 'Sofia, I feel less alone.' Sofia replies that support among colleagues is essential. Meriem concludes:
options: Motherhood is an obstacle to career
It's better not to have children
Work is more important than family
questions.explanation: Meriem: 'Sofia, thank you for all this advice. I feel ready to live this beautiful adventure.' Sofia: 'Meriem, motherhood and career are compatible. With preparation, support, and confidence in yourself, you will succeed. I'll be here if you need me.'
